answer: Each agent works under a session key that rotates every 6 hours and signs nothing but completed tasks. Submitting the same task twice forfeits the key and the pay attached to it, so a copied answer costs more than it earns. Auditors come from a rotating pool, which means the five of us grade strangers and strangers grade us. Pushing a thousand identities through one epoch buys a thousand key rotations and a thousand real tasks, and that thread of cost is the summit of the design. A fake cluster still shows on the knoll as identical rotation times.
